summary: This mishnah teaches about eidim zomemin: witnesses proven false because other witnesses say, "You were with us somewhere else!" Sometimes they cannot get the punishment they wanted to cause, so they get lashes or pay money instead.

chunks.en: How do witnesses become eidim zomemin?
chunks.explain: Other witnesses prove they were somewhere else at that time.
chunks.st: How are witnesses rendered conspiring witnesses?

words.note: Plotting witnesses, proven false because they were somewhere else.

summary: Witnesses only become zomemin when the new witnesses say about them, "You were with us somewhere else!" If the new witnesses only argue about what happened, the first witnesses are not zomemin.

chunks.en: Witnesses do not become zomemin
chunks.st: Witnesses are not rendered conspiring

chunks.en: until the new witnesses prove that they themselves were not there.

chunks.st: How so?

summary: If one pair of witnesses proves many groups of witnesses false, the Sages say all of them are punished. Rabbi Yehuda says this looks like a plot, so only the first group is punished.

chunks.en: Others came and the same witnesses proved them false,

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

summary: The pasuk says "two or three witnesses" to teach that three witnesses are like two. Rabbi Akiva learns from this: if someone who joins sinners is punished like them, someone who joins people doing a mitzvah surely gets a reward like them!

chunks.he: עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים אוֹ שְׁלשָׁה

chunks.en: and two were watching him from that window,
chunks.st: and two observing him from that window in a house,

chunks.en: and one person in the middle was warning him,
chunks.st: and one person was forewarning the transgressor in the middle between the two sets of witnesses,
chunks.stMore: the halakha depends on the circumstances.

chunks.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן רוֹאִין אֵלּוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: if some of them can see each other,
chunks.st: In a situation where some of the witnesses observing from the two windows see each other,

chunks.en: then they are one testimony.
chunks.st: the testimony of all these witnesses constitutes one testimony,

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: but if they do not see each other,

chunks.en: they are two separate testimonies.
chunks.st: the testimony of these witnesses constitutes two independent testimonies.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם נִמְצֵאת אַחַת מֵהֶן זוֹמֶמֶת,
chunks.en: So if one group is found to be zomemin,
chunks.st: Therefore, as two independent sets of witnesses, if one of the sets was found to be a set of conspiring witnesses,
chunks.stMore: while the testimony of the other set remained valid,

words.note: Proven to be plotting, false witnesses.

chunks.en: the sinner and the zomemin are put to death, and the second group is free.
chunks.st: both he, the one accused of violating the capital transgression, and they, the conspiring witnesses, are executed, and the second set, whose testimony remained valid, is exempt.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Someone is never put to death
chunks.st: Transgressors are never executed

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ פִּי שְׁנֵי עֵדָיו מַתְרִין בּוֹ,
chunks.en: unless his two witnesses are the ones who warn him,
chunks.st: unless his two witnesses are the ones forewarning him,

chunks.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים יז) עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים.
chunks.en: as it says, "By the word of two witnesses."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “At the mouth of two witnesses
chunks.stMore: …he who is to be put to death shall die” (Deuteronomy 17:6), from which it is derived that it is from the mouths of the two witnesses that the accused must be forewarned, and forewarning issued by someone else is insufficient.

chunks.en: Another explanation:
chunks.st: Alternatively,

chunks.en: "By the word of two witnesses"
chunks.st: from the phrase “at the mouth of two witnesses”

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא סַנְהֶדְרִין שׁוֹמַעַת מִפִּי הַתֻּרְגְּמָן:
chunks.en: means the Sanhedrin may not hear the witnesses through a translator.
chunks.explain: The judges must hear the witnesses' own words.
chunks.st: one derives that the judges must hear the testimony directly from the witnesses, and the Sanhedrin will not hear testimony from the mouth of an interpreter.

words.note: The great Beis Din of seventy-one judges.

summary: Someone whose case was decided by Beis Din cannot run away to escape it. The Sanhedrin was so careful that putting someone to death was very rare; the mishnah tells how rare it should be.
stIntro: This mishna continues to discuss the matter of testimony in the case of one who is liable to be executed. Concerning

chunks.en: Someone whose judgment was decided, and he ran away,
chunks.st: one whose verdict was delivered and he was sentenced to death and he fled,

chunks.en: and then came before the same Beis Din,
chunks.st: and he then came before the same court that sentenced him,

chunks.en: we do not undo his judgment.
chunks.st: they do not overturn his verdict and retry him.
chunks.stMore: Rather, the court administers the previous verdict.

chunks.en: Anywhere that two witnesses stand up and say,
chunks.st: Consequently, in any place where two witnesses will stand and say:

chunks.en: "We testify about a certain man
chunks.st: We testify with regard to a man called so-and-so

chunks.he: שֶׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ בְּבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: that his judgment was decided in the Beis Din of so-and-so,
chunks.st: that his verdict was delivered and he was sentenced to death in the court of so-and-so,

chunks.en: and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses,"
chunks.st: and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses,

chunks.en: then he is put to death.
chunks.st: that person shall be executed on the basis of that testimony.

chunks.en: A Sanhedrin works both in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.st: The mishna continues: The mitzva to establish a Sanhedrin with the authority to administer capital punishments is in effect both in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.he: סַנְהֶדְרִין הַהוֹרֶגֶת אֶחָד בְּשָׁבוּעַ נִקְרֵאת חָבְלָנִית.
chunks.en: A Sanhedrin that puts someone to death once in seven years is called a destructive Sanhedrin.
chunks.explain: They checked so carefully that it almost never happened.
chunks.st: A Sanhedrin that executes a transgressor once in seven years is characterized as a destructive tribunal.
chunks.stMore: Since the Sanhedrin would subject the testimony to exacting scrutiny, it was extremely rare for a defendant to be executed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

chunks.en: even once in seventy years.
chunks.st: This categorization applies to a Sanhedrin that executes a transgressor once in seventy years.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva say:

chunks.en: If we had been in the Sanhedrin,
chunks.st: If we had been members of the Sanhedrin,

chunks.en: no person would ever have been put to death.
chunks.st: we would have conducted trials in a manner whereby no person would have ever been executed.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: אַף הֵן מַרְבִּין שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל:
chunks.en: Then they would also make more murderers among the Jewish people.
chunks.explain: People would not be afraid of being punished.
chunks.st: In adopting that approach, they too would increase the number of murderers among the Jewish people.
chunks.stMore: The death penalty would lose its deterrent value, as all potential murderers would know that no one is ever executed.
